title: From Closed to Mighty: How GTP-Induced Allosteric Dynamics, Dimerization, and Membrane Binding Transform a Bacterial Dynamin-like Protein.
authors: Schumann, Wibke; Bundschuh, Bastian F; Loschwitz, Jennifer; Strodel, Birgit
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过全原子增强采样MD模拟揭示细菌dynamin样蛋白GTP诱导的闭合-开放构象转变机制，核心聚焦蛋白质构象动态与膜重塑，方法为物理模拟，与课题高度相关。
abstract: Dynamins, crucial GTPases involved in membrane remodeling, play key roles in processes like endocytosis and membrane fission. While their importance is well-established, the precise dynamics of their conformational changes remain unclear. This study investigates the bacterial dynamin-like protein (BDLP) from Nostoc punctiforme, which undergoes a dramatic closed-to-open transition upon GTP binding. Using standard and enhanced all-atom molecular dynamics simulations, we map this transition, revealing a complex energetic landscape. The initial barrier arises from disruption of salt bridges formed by the GTPase domain with the trunk and paddle, setting off the main hinge motion. Subsequent conformational changes involve further hinge motions and lateral shearing to minimize electrostatic forces. Notably, GTP binding accelerates the transition by 5 orders of magnitude through an allosteric mechanism. Our multiscale simulations of 37.1 mus accumulated simulation time show that BDLP dimerization and membrane binding are necessary to initiate the stabilization of the open conformation. These findings provide crucial insights into BDLP's membrane remodeling mechanism, advancing our understanding of dynamin dynamics.
abstract_zh: 发动蛋白（Dynamins）是参与膜重塑的关键GTP酶，在内吞作用和膜分裂等过程中发挥重要作用。尽管其重要性已得到充分确认，但其构象变化的具体动力学仍不清楚。本研究探讨了来自点状念珠藻（Nostoc punctiforme）的细菌发动蛋白样蛋白（BDLP），该蛋白在GTP结合时经历剧烈的闭合到开放转变。利用标准和增强的全原子分子动力学模拟，我们绘制了这一转变过程，揭示了一个复杂的能量景观。初始能垒源于GTP酶结构域与主干和桨叶形成的盐桥断裂，从而触发主要铰链运动。随后的构象变化涉及进一步的铰链运动和横向剪切，以最小化静电力。值得注意的是，GTP结合通过变构机制将转变加速了5个数量级。我们累计37.1微秒模拟时间的多尺度模拟表明，BDLP二聚化和膜结合是启动开放构象稳定化的必要条件。这些发现为BDLP的膜重塑机制提供了关键见解，推进了我们对发动蛋白动力学的理解。
